body:
I think the difference from #110474 is that this was added. Are there any other changes? Is a new benchmark comparison possible?

If https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110474#pullrequestreview-3302152139 issue was due to multiple same AnimationNode resources being instantiated and placed, then the fix to manage each resource's instance makes sense. I confirmed that this no longer causes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110474#pullrequestreview-3302152139 issue.

However, since I recall past issues similar to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110506, I'm a bit concerned about whether using thread_local is appropriate. Testing in a project editing scenes containing a large number of AnimationTree instances might be necessary.

Also, I have some concerns regarding code readability. Passing instance pointers as arguments is indeed safe, but since there should be never occur to access different ProcessState and AnimationNodeInstance within a single AnimationNode like:
```
double length_a = instance_a.get_parameter(current_length);
double length_b = instance_b.get_parameter(current_length);
```
, so it always `p_instance.get_parameter()`, it would be ideal if there is a way to omit them, same with old code. This would significantly reduce the number of lines requiring modification. Do you have any ideas @lyuma @SaracenOne?

If there are no other way, I assume it can be accepted depending on the benchmark improvement. In other words, we want a benchmark comparison before and after, focusing solely on changes to the AnimationTree instance, excluding any other changes. This was one reason why I suggested separating the PR.

body:
> No compatibility methods registered because it breaks C# builds.

What do you mean by this? That since there's a compile-time error, there's no risk of breaking at runtime?

If yes, that misses the point: this is primarily about GDExtension (as indicated by file path), although it covers C# as well. GDExtensions must remain _binary compatible_, i.e. an extension compiled against Godot 4.1 must still run without UB under Godot 4.5.

In this case that is true because `float` and `double` are represented the same in GDExtension's FFI (namely as `double`), but that means you should change the reasoning here.

Please read again what I wrote -- you don't need compat methods here, but you need to provide a reason _why_ the binary compatibility is OK as-is.

"C# does not compile" is the symptom, not the cause. The cause is the same FFI repr (see my previous response).
SNAME
SNAME here and same in other places with "default_color"

If an animation loops, is `seeked` true? (will `reset_cursors()` be called?)
If not, it may be expensive to rerun the linear scan to the beginning.

We should test to make sure we are not running an expensive seek

```
#if DEBUG_ENABLED
if unlikely ((i-hint) > 200 || (i-hint) < -200) {
print an error to report an issue so we can see if we're failing the find with hint.
}
#endif 
```
and same in the other cases.
